ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The attached diagram shows a square of side length 2a with its center marked O. There is one wire cross-section at each corner. The top-left and bottom-right wires are marked with dots, indicating current out of the page. The top-right and bottom-left wires are marked with crosses, indicating current into the page. Reasoning: Put O at the origin and the four corners at (-a, a), (a, a), (-a, -a), and (a, -a). The center is the same distance a*sqrt(2) from every wire, so the magnetic-field magnitudes from the four wires at O are equal. By the right-hand rule, an out-of-page current produces counterclockwise field lines, and an into-page current produces clockwise field lines. At O, the field from the top-left out-of-page wire points northeast, while the field from the bottom-right out-of-page wire points southwest, so these two equal vectors cancel. The field from the top-right into-page wire points northwest, while the field from the bottom-left into-page wire points southeast, so these two equal vectors also cancel. Therefore the vector sum of the four magnetic fields at O is zero.
